title: Conjectured tight weighted Frobenius norm bounds for matrix commutators
statement:
Let $\omega \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ be a positive matrix, and let $\lambda_{\rm M}$, $\lambda_{\rm m}$, and $\lambda_{\rm sm}$ denote respectively its largest, smallest, and second smallest eigenvalues. For matrices $A,B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$, write $[A,B]=AB-BA$, and let $\|\cdot\|_\omega$ and $\|\cdot\|$ denote the weighted and ordinary Frobenius norms used in the paper.

**Conjectured tight bounds.** The tight bounds for cases (i), (ii), and (iv) are respectively

$$
\|[A,B]\|_\omega \leq \sqrt{\frac{\lambda_{\rm m}+\lambda_{\rm sm}}{\lambda_{\rm m}\lambda_{\rm sm}}}\,\|A\|_\omega\|B\|_\omega,
$$

$$
\|[A,B]\|_\omega \leq \sqrt{\frac{\lambda_{\rm m}+\lambda_{\rm M}}{\lambda_{\rm m}}}\,\|A\|_\omega\|B\|,
$$

and

$$
\|[A,B]\|\leq \sqrt{\frac{\lambda_{\rm m}+\lambda_{\rm sm}}{\lambda_{\rm m}^2\lambda_{\rm sm}}}\,\|A\|_\omega\|B\|_\omega.
$$

In each case, the bound is tight: there are nonzero matrices $A$ and $B$ attaining equality. These claims are motivated by numerical optimizations; the paper presents them as conjectures, so their general validity remains open.

source_name: Aina Mayumi, Gen Kimura, Hiromichi Ohno and Dariusz Chruściński, “Böttcher-Wenzel inequality for weighted Frobenius norms and its application to quantum physics”, arXiv:2403.04199 (2024).

progress.label: Open
progress.tldr: The three proposed sharp bounds remain conjectures: numerical tests and low-dimensional special cases support them, but no general proof or counterexample has been reported.
progress.summary:
A 2024 paper asks whether three eigenvalue-dependent commutator inequalities for weighted Frobenius norms are universally valid and sharp. The proposed constants depend on the smallest, second-smallest, and largest eigenvalues of the positive weight matrix.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.04199) · [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2403.04199)*

**Known results**

- The paper proves the corresponding tight bounds for cases $(iii)$ and $(v)$.
- For the conjectured cases $(i)$, $(ii)$, and $(iv)$, proofs are given when $n=2$ and in certain special cases.
- Numerical optimization agrees with the conjectured constants for randomly generated weights through $n=15$.


**2024 conjecture and subsequent status**

The paper presents cases $(i)$ and $(ii)$ as conjectures, with case $(iv)$ derived from case $(i)$, and supplies equality examples. The scan found no later proof, counterexample, withdrawal, retraction, or independent verification.

*[arxiv.gg](https://arxiv.gg/abs/2403.04199)*

Current status (as of August 2026): the bounds for cases $(iii)$ and $(v)$ are settled, while the proposed tight bounds for cases $(i)$, $(ii)$, and $(iv)$ remain open.
